layer: Moon height (moon.html, optional): What LRO measured: height
kind: derived page files from a measurement-derived grid (laser altimetry compiled by the LOLA team); not live

source.citation: Smith, D.E.; Neumann, G.A. (2023). Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter LOLA Processed (RDR) Data Products. NASA PDS. https://doi.org/10.17189/tnyt-7007
source.data_period: 2009-07-13T17:33:17 to 2016-11-29T05:48:19 (through mission phase LRO_ES_52); product created 2017-09-15
source.quantity: height relative to a 1737.4 km reference sphere (km, float32); not a geoid height, not altitude
source.grid: 1440 x 720, 0.25 deg spacing, equirectangular, pixel registered, planetocentric; 0-360 E from column 0; frame MEAN EARTH/POLAR AXIS OF DE421
source.rights: PDS Geosciences FAQ (read 26 Nov 2026): 'Data sets archived in the PDS are in the public domain'; cite appropriately (bundle DOI + LIDVID)

comparison_product_for_withheld_rows.finding: agrees with LDEM_4_FLOAT within one 0.5 m step in every cell of rows 2-719; rows 0-1 disagree in 1,038 cells by up to 1,423 m (docs/research/moon-lro-science/SAMPLES.md)

withheld.rule: rows 0-1 (north of 89.5 N) stored as -32768 and drawn as a grey cap
withheld.wording: Values north of 89.5°N are withheld because inconsistencies were found in the source products.

ldem4-m-R1.i16.gz.format: int16 little-endian, row-major 720 x 1440, source order (row 0 at 90 N, column 0 at 0 E), whole metres rounded in float64 (half to even), -32768 = withheld; gzip -9, mtime 0

ldem4-colour-R1.png.format: 2048 x 1024 indexed PNG, 0 deg at the centre; each pixel the colour of the 0.25 deg cell containing its centre; one-hue blue ramp from -9 km (dark) to +11 km (light), 254 colours (about 79 m per step); withheld cap grey #8c8c8c

review_cadence: check for a newer version yearly and at each build (PDS errata, LOLA Data Node listing)
page_rules: fetched only when the user switches height on; both files checked (compressed and decompressed pins) before use; readout gives the containing cell's value, no interpolation; rounding to the metre is precision, not accuracy
